records.title: Republican state Sen. Taffy Howard faces campaign finance crime allegation
records.description: A complaint against state Republican Senator Taffy Howard alleges improper campaign contributions violated state campaign finance law.

records.title: U.S. Supreme Court cases deal with cost of climate change, discrimination, death penalty
records.description: Mike Thompson previews U.S. Supreme Court arguments, from climate change accountability to habeas corpus in a death penalty case.

records.title: Officials say beloved Black Hills bald eagle died from lead poisoning
records.description: Hope, a famous bald eagle which roosted in Rapid City’s Canyon Lake neighborhood for nearly a decade, has died. An autopsy confirmed the cause was lead poisoning.

records.title: South Dakota's economy buoyed by federal ag assistance, state economic council says
records.description: South Dakota’s economy is a mixed bag, officials say. Part of that is the fact that farmers are getting a chunk of their income from the government, not markets.

records.title: South Dakota receives share of nationwide GM settlement over driver data misuse
records.description: South Dakota is receiving $2.6 million dollars in a settlement from General Motors over allegations the company illegally sold consumers’ data.

records.title: 'Yearslong process' to reduce state's recidivism rate requires money, culture changes
records.description: If South Dakota wants to see real change in its prison system as it pursues a stronger push for rehabilitation, it has a few things to clean up. While many are already underway administratively, it’s going to take time and cost some money, according to a report created for a legislative task force studying these issues.

records.title: South Dakota receives share of nationwide GM settlement over driver data misuse
records.description: South Dakota is receiving $2.6 million dollars in a settlement from General Motors over allegations the company illegally sold consumers’ data.

records.title: Private lending is fueling the AI boom. How might that change the U.S. financial system?
records.description: Banks have grown, but non-bank lending has grown even faster. Joe Santos explains how private lending fuels innovation while opening the door to vulnerabilities.

records.title: Recent rain means delayed harvest but better spring for farmers, expert says
records.description: After what’s been a dry year, precipitation has increased recently in parts of South Dakota. It brings both short-term headaches and potentially long-term benefits to farmers.

records.title: State habitat fund receives nearly $8 million for grassland restoration initiative
records.description: A South Dakota organization is receiving nearly $8 million from the USDA to support a statewide grassland program.

records.title: AP: Rhoden wins South Dakota gubernatorial race
records.description: Republican Gov. Larry Rhoden has won four more years in the state’s highest office after defeating Democrat Dan Ahlers in the race for South Dakota governor.

records.title: Jackley wins race for U.S. House, AP projects
records.description: Republican Marty Jackley has won the race for South Dakota's lone seat in the U.S. House of Representatives.

records.title: Thwarting communism, 'flipping SD blue' and healthcare: What's driving some South Dakotans to polls
records.description: Election voting is underway in the state. South Dakotans are hitting polls across the state to vote on candidates for federal and state-level contests. They’re also voting on Constitutional amendments. SDPB visited some polls in the state to see what's driving voters this year.

records.title: Productive struggle is key to learning. AI wants to eliminate it
records.description: Teachers Gina Benz and Jackie Wilber unpack the latest research into AI in the classroom, including the role of human teachers in understanding when students are working in the "sweet spot" for learning.

records.title: Polls now closed in South Dakota for midterm elections
records.description: Tuesday is election day. South Dakota voters have several big decisions in front of them for this year’s midterm.

records.title: Rapid City passes first school bond effort since Nixon Presidency
records.description: For the first time since the early 1970s, Rapid City has approved a school bond vote. Officials say this bond ensures each school has air conditioning, a new school can be built and modern security measures can be implemented districtwide.

records.title: Early returns of new laws show voters rejecting sales tax shift options
records.description: Several efforts to implement new sales taxes fail at the local level in South Dakota. Two involved counties rejecting a sales tax to offset property tax and another saw a city vote down a tax to subsidize childcare development.

records.title: Voters reject Medicaid, constitutional amendment changes on ballot
records.description: South Dakota voters approved two constitutional amendments on the ballot in Tuesday's election while rejecting two others.

records.title: Thune says Senate Republicans won't 'stand idly by' in face of Democrats' new majority
records.description: South Dakota Republican U.S. Sen. John Thune plans to make a bid to continue leading his party in the Senate, though if successful, his title is set to change.

records.title: For the first time in years, Democrats gain seats in South Dakota Legislature
records.description: While Democrats didn’t win any statewide races in South Dakota, they did pick up some seats in the state Legislature.

records.title: For both GOP & Dems, it was the best of nights, the worst of nights
records.byline: By Lori Walsh, C.J. Keene, Jackson Dircks, Jackie Hendry
records.description: South Dakota Republicans won big at home but mourned a shifting national landscape. State Democrats won little at home, but danced joyfully at a blue wave that swept the U.S. SDPB reporters explore the tale of two parties.

records.title: While SD Democrats don't win statewide, candidates draw hope from other states flipping
records.description: South Dakota Democrats will have to wait another two years if they want to see a Democrat win a statewide office.

records.title: AP: Rounds wins U.S. Senate reelection bid
records.description: Republican Sen. Mike Rounds is retaining his seat representing South Dakota in the U.S. Senate.

records.title: Rapid City adjusts general public comment at city council meetings
records.description: Business will change for Rapid City Common Council meetings. In a shift, general public comment will now take place at the end of the docket rather than the top.

records.title: Second year funding delayed for Rural Health Transformation Program
records.description: According to a report from KFF Health News, state leaders received an email on Oct. 30 alerting them to the second-year funding announcement delay.

records.title: State DCI report sheds light on what led up to shooting of Deputy Frank
records.description: New details on the death of Minnehaha Sheriff’s Deputy Katherine Frank have been released following a state-led investigation. Among the findings — an officer was deemed justified in firing his weapon at the suspect who shot Frank.

records.title: While 'blue wave' didn't reach South Dakota statewide races, Dems see promise in legislative results
records.description: South Dakota Democratic candidates running for statewide office got swept by Republicans. But in legislative races Dems pushed to flip seats for the first time in years, cutting into one of the country’s darkest red supermajorities.

records.title: 'American Pope' biography offers insights into Leo XIV's take on AI and human dignity
records.description: NPR's Daniel Burke and Scott Detrow discuss their biography of Robert Prevost and his journey from the south side of Chicago to Vatican City.

records.title: Frontline's 'Scammed' investigates the underbelly of a global scamming industry
records.description: Since the pandemic, the scamming industry has metastasized into a global network of relentless attacks. Frontline's Martha Mendoza explains how it works, who suffers, and how Americans are fighting back.
